“I would tell prospective sponsors or supporters that every dollar used by a student means so much more than just that dollar. The work each and every student puts into becoming an NMSC scholar makes the scholarship they receive an important part of their academic motivation. NMSC is one of the few organizations that allows students to work towards scholarships solely with their academic ability, which makes receiving the scholarship that much more valuable. The recipients of NMSC scholarships have their lives changed beyond just the money they receive.”
Preston B. Grooms, 2021 National Merit Florida State University Scholarship

Published: 4/18/2022 8:40 AM  
Scholar Snapshot featuring Emma R. Teff  
Emma R. Teff, a recipient of a 2021 National Merit $2500 Scholarship, is pictured here competing in the dressage division of the North American Youth Championships in 2019, representing USA Region 1. "I am an avid equestrian and am very passionate about dressage, which is like ballet or figure skating on horseback. I have been riding dressage since I was 10 years old," says Emma. In addition to her academic success, her equestrian achievements have meant the most to Emma. She says, "Winning a Perseverance Award from an equestrian program meant the most to me because it was a reminder that having a good attitude in any circumstance pays off."  
Read More  
Published: 4/11/2022 9:11 AM  
Giving Back, featuring Nikhita S. Mudium  
"The most stubborn and fragile organ in our body, the brain and the nervous system, allow us to care for each other and ourselves. However, the brain and its tissues are also the least understood, and when they malfunction because of an injury or disorder, it is devastating," says Nikhita S. Mudium, a 2021 National Merit $2500 Scholarship recipient, about her chosen field of study. Nikhita is attending the University of Alabama at Birmingham, where she plans to major in neuroscience and public health. "I chose to study neuroscience, because I want to be part of unraveling the mystery of the nervous system and its disorders … By also studying public health, I want to increase access to health and lower health disparities that are present across many races, socioeconomic levels, and gender."

Published: 4/11/2022 9:08 AM  
Quote of the Day - Carter W. Berg  
“It seems like everything in my life is related to conservation biology. I recently went on a backpacking trip on Slough Creek in Yellowstone National Park and had the wonderful opportunity to catch native Yellowstone cutthroat trout surrounded by towering mountains. However, the future of the trout are in jeopardy due to hybridization from invasive rainbow trout. I would love to help preserve this population of native trout in the future.”

Carter W. Berg, 2021 National Merit Montana State University – Bozeman Scholarship
Published: 4/11/2022 9:06 AM  
Post-Graduate Plans featuring Sydney Marchando  
Sydney Marchando, a 2017 National Merit Black & Veatch Scholarship recipient, was a pitcher on the varsity softball team all four years while attending Colorado School of Mines, as well as serving as the president of the Student-Athlete Advisory Committee. This position position allowed her to coordinate and volunteer with initiatives that improved access to sports for all, including Special Olympics Colorado competitions on campus and A Precious Child Colorado sports equipment donation drives. During her undergraduate career, Sydney also volunteered with local elementary school students through a reading program sponsored by the Student-Athlete Advisory Committee. She says, "These experiences solidified my desire to pursue a career where I can continue to help people and improve my community."

Scholar Snapshot featuring Olivia A. Luzzio  
Olivia A. Luzzio, a 2017 National Merit Washington and Lee University Scholarship recipient, is pictured on the Speaker's Balcony at the U.S. Capitol Building during an internship in Washington, DC. Olivia says, "During spring of my sophomore year, I had the chance to intern with the Business Council for Sustainable Energy (BCSE), which is a business association advocating for clean energy solutions in Washington, DC. The chance to work in environmental policy led me to take more courses in environmental economics and sustainability in college, and ultimately led to my interest in pursuing environmental law."

Quote of the Day - Adam Allen Swartz  
“A short while ago I read an article about a company that develops floating solar panel arrays designed to float on large bodies of water. It seems like a fairly simple and straightforward concept, but the impacts are huge. This project led to a resurgence of motivation for me, as it showed me that I, too, can come up with ideas involving environmental engineering or mechanical engineering that can positively impact the world around me.”
Adam Allen Swartz, 2021 National Merit $2500 Scholarship

Published: 4/4/2022 9:51 AM  
Scholar Q&A: Mia J. Rauer, 2021 National Merit $2500 Scholarship  
Q. Where are you attending college, and what do you plan to major in? Why did you choose this field of study?
A. I am majoring in sustainable environmental design at the University of California Berkeley. I chose this field of study because I am deeply passionate about the environment, and design is a wonderful way for me to integrate my various passions, including physics, art, creativity, social justice, and environmental consciousness. Despite feeling overwhelmed at the destructive effects of climate change I continue to witness, environmental design empowers me to make grassroots change, filling me with optimism that we can and will transition to a sustainable future.

Published: 3/28/2022 9:08 AM  
Scholar Snapshot, featuring Luke Peart  
Luke Peart, recipient of a 2021 State Farm Companies Foundation Scholarship, is pictured here tightening bolts 80 feet in the air while constructing a grain leg for his family farm, Peart Farms Ltd. He says:
Having been heavily involved in agricultural organizations throughout high school and having been employed by a family farm, I chose to study agriculture without hesitation. Farming is a unique industry in that it is the basis of our civilization; everyone needs to eat so there will always be a need for agriculture. I hope that in the coming years I might be a part of the generation of agriculturalists who eliminate food insecurity in the United States and the world.

Published: 4/18/2022 8:40 AM  
Scholar Snapshot featuring Emma R. Teff  
Emma R. Teff, a recipient of a 2021 National Merit $2500 Scholarship, is pictured here competing in the dressage division of the North American Youth Championships in 2019, representing USA Region 1. "I am an avid equestrian and am very passionate about dressage, which is like ballet or figure skating on horseback. I have been riding dressage since I was 10 years old," says Emma. In addition to her academic success, her equestrian achievements have meant the most to Emma. She says, "Winning a Perseverance Award from an equestrian program meant the most to me because it was a reminder that having a good attitude in any circumstance pays off."

Giving Back, featuring Nikhita S. Mudium  
"The most stubborn and fragile organ in our body, the brain and the nervous system, allow us to care for each other and ourselves. However, the brain and its tissues are also the least understood, and when they malfunction because of an injury or disorder, it is devastating," says Nikhita S. Mudium, a 2021 National Merit $2500 Scholarship recipient, about her chosen field of study. Nikhita is attending the University of Alabama at Birmingham, where she plans to major in neuroscience and public health. "I chose to study neuroscience, because I want to be part of unraveling the mystery of the nervous system and its disorders … By also studying public health, I want to increase access to health and lower health disparities that are present across many races, socioeconomic levels, and gender."

Quote of the Day - Carter W. Berg  
“It seems like everything in my life is related to conservation biology. I recently went on a backpacking trip on Slough Creek in Yellowstone National Park and had the wonderful opportunity to catch native Yellowstone cutthroat trout surrounded by towering mountains. However, the future of the trout are in jeopardy due to hybridization from invasive rainbow trout. I would love to help preserve this population of native trout in the future.”

Sydney Marchando, a 2017 National Merit Black & Veatch Scholarship recipient, was a pitcher on the varsity softball team all four years while attending Colorado School of Mines, as well as serving as the president of the Student-Athlete Advisory Committee. Q. Where are you attending college, and what do you plan to major in? Why did you choose this field of study?
A. I am majoring in sustainable environmental design at the University of California Berkeley. I chose this field of study because I am deeply passionate about the environment, and design is a wonderful way for me to integrate my various passions, including physics, art, creativity, social justice, and environmental consciousness. Despite feeling overwhelmed at the destructive effects of climate change I continue to witness, environmental design empowers me to make grassroots change, filling me with optimism that we can and will transition to a sustainable future.

Luke Peart, recipient of a 2021 State Farm Companies Foundation Scholarship, is pictured here tightening bolts 80 feet in the air while constructing a grain leg for his family farm, Peart Farms Ltd. He says:
Having been heavily involved in agricultural organizations throughout high school and having been employed by a family farm, I chose to study agriculture without hesitation. Farming is a unique industry in that it is the basis of our civilization; everyone needs to eat so there will always be a need for agriculture. I hope that in the coming years I might be a part of the generation of agriculturalists who eliminate food insecurity in the United States and the world.

"I collaborated with student volunteers to provide warm meals for local Gainesville citizens facing homelessness at [an outreach at] our city hall," Aidan explains. "I collaborated with student volunteers to provide warm meals for local Gainesville citizens facing homelessness at [an outreach at] our city hall," Aidan explains. “Earning a National Merit Scholarship opened doors I never thought possible. Coming from Louisiana, I initially assumed I’d stay close to home for college. But the scholarship gave me the financial freedom and confidence to explore options beyond state lines. It became the first step in applying to the University of Arkansas, where I was later awarded an Honors College Fellowship. That opportunity changed everything. Without the National Merit Scholarship, I may never have found the school that truly felt like home or been able to pursue my passion for computer science in such a supportive and challenging environment. It set me on the path to grow not only academically, but personally, and helped turn a distant dream into a reality.”
Evan M. Bonar, 2025 National Merit University of Arkansas, Fayetteville Scholarship

Julia Ingram, recipient of a 2021 National Merit University of Florida Scholarship, earned her bachelor of arts degree in biology. Inspired by University of Florida (UF) faculty to "always learn more about the human body," Julia pursued numerous opportunities in her field. Her first internship was at the UF Health Hereditary Cancer Program as a genetic counseling assistant. "I spoke with patients before and after meeting with the genetic counselor, helping them navigate complex emotions," she explains. Additionally, Julia was a research assistant for the Center for Inflammation Science and Systems Medicine at The Herbert Wertheim UF Scripps Institute for Biomedical Innovation and Technology.
